conclusion: Boot to READY with domain 4 OFF at entry takes 4,628 us (5 ticks as the model rounds): the owner reads DCDC2 at its first step and publishes it verified at 2.0 ms; the call it wakes runs the pass and the domain-4 request; the call that the row's ON answer wakes runs the enable table, LOCK and the local open table, ending at 2.63 ms; the call at the last tick before the settle ends spins to its end, 2 ms later, reads back and returns READY. With domain 4 ON at entry, as both boards read at boot, it takes 4,615 us. The 2 ms vendor settle stays and ends exactly. The PMIC provider moves one register per transaction, so the 12 verification reads cannot merge into a multi-byte transfer without a provider change, which is not made. The CPU-side NPU setup has nothing to move into the settle. The adapter builds the MMU tables before the scheduler starts; the convolution images also build both command streams then, while the runtime images build a model's stream when a client loads it through the active service, after OPEN. The bootstrap stream's integrity check stays immediately before the device fetches it.

narrative: Two checks failed on the base for reasons outside the record change. (1) npu-single-core.py --retention-only stopped at its third case because a733_smp_device_preparation_admitted returned 0: since the boot began preparing the local pools in platform_init, a kernel critical section runs there before the scheduler; in the single-core port uxPortSetInterruptMask masks IRQs through the priority mask and clears DAIF.I, so the admission's DAIF check refused (DAIF.I is cleared when uxPortSetInterruptMask returns, so any later critical section before the scheduler clears it again). platform_init now sets DAIF.I after the preparation, and the admission in a733_smp_diagnostic_start runs before any task is created and must stay there. The board image would have refused in the same way. (2) accelerator-providers.py returned reason 5 from a733_npu_application_init because the check skipped that same boot preparation, so the NPU reservation read a NULL pool; the check now runs both pool preparations first and models the port's critical sections they enter. The apps/accelerators project failed to link at 66e0ef6: the single-core NPU image and the accelerator image reported every FreeRTOS tasks.c symbol undefined, because commit f4a272f patched tasks.c for the SMP base, its filter removes the patched copy from single-core images, and it added the kernel's own tasks.c to two single-core recipes but not to cmake/a733-npu-single-core.cmake; the one line added there makes all three images link. checks/storage-read-native.py refuses images in which two compilation units define different structures with one tag (a733_pmic.c and a733_power_domains.c both define struct profile); each check passes layout_names to Image with the structures it reads, as checks/displayport-admission.py does, so no source is renamed. Check changes: npu-application-clock-reference.py drives the image's sequencer through its register pass with six reference cases (refused cases make no write; admitted ones write the enable table, first the gate enable at CCU+0x1920); npu-stop-native.py uses a layout reader restricted to no structure and adds refused domain-4 policy and delay-row writes and the PLL gate rules (fourteen cases); npu-single-core.py --retention-only uses a restricted layout reader and a reduced-record fixture at version 3; accelerator-providers.py checks the view of the application's one GPU/PCK manager, the startup's borrowed providers and its single domain-4 row, and that a domain-4 fault leaves the shared providers live; npu-board-providers.py is new (see memory placement in the design).

hypothesis: The NPU board image starts the NPU, runs catalogue model 0 against its pinned 72-byte reference, and closes with controller state CLOSED
prediction:
The first NPU attempt also needs the preparer's authenticated conditions:

- Exclusive CPU, memory and DMA ownership, with remote writers excluded.
- NPU SRAM confinement and drain ownership, plus disabled, inactive, clear INTID 97.
- Exclusive PLL_NPU consumers and writers, with independent DRAM clock sources.
- Stable DCDC2 at 800 mV and inherited PMIC pin ownership.
- The extended DDR reservation and a USB reference matching the cached-SMP cold-entry profile.

Runtime readbacks can reject changed settings but do not establish these
external conditions.

After those conditions are established, the smallest inference attempt uses
catalogue model 0, one upload, one SUBMIT, a byte comparison with its pinned
72-byte reference, RETURN and CLOSE. Freeze the image, session and evidence
before launch. The host consumes and durably records the terminal zero-length
packet when a response occupies a whole number of USB packets, including
every 64-byte header at full speed. It reports success only after all output
files match, CLOSE reports controller state CLOSED, and the original USB
instance remains within the capture deadline. Twenty modeled host cases
exercise those boundaries and the actual supervisor
(`checks/npu-board-capture.py`).

Retain resources for the prescribed whole-board power removal,
and stop communication after the first failure. CLOSE stops the NPU locally; USB0 remains active until the
20-second session deadline. This image has no normal ROM-return path.
The single-core `apps/npu-finite` consumer separately implements verified
quiescence and normal ROM return while retaining the NPU power domain.
That return implementation does not cover the SMP board providers. Current board recovery and admission state belong in the
[handoff](../handoff.md).

Board evidence planned (one session per whole-board power removal):

1. The register-pass words and domain-4 status after boot, against the
   constants, and the measured PLL_NPU lock time.
2. Domain-4 time to ON through the owner, a status trace, the reads of
   `0xc00`–`0xc10` before and after the delay-row write
   (docs/power-domains.md, board evidence), and whether the final local
   state holds without the 2 ms settle.
3. Boot to READY in the board image, ShuffleNetV2 output equal to the SDK
   reference, and a LOAD that switches the slot between two catalogue models.
4. One INTID 97 interrupt per job on core 1.
5. USB0 throughput and power-service step durations while jobs run.
6. The extended-memory reservation evidence that
   docs/device-memory-capacity.md requires.

Estimated, not a target: one ShuffleNetV2 inference over USB0, upload to output read, about 40 ticks (150,528 input bytes are 294 high-speed packets, 30 ticks at 10 packets per tick; the 6.58 ms slot, 7 ticks; one tick for each of SUBMIT, READ and RETURN).
conclusion: Not yet run on the board: this image has not run on a board. The physical entry needs a qualified eight-core entry, a coherent extended DDR reservation and matching recovery evidence on the target board, which a single-core USB result cannot supply.
narrative: Preconditions and outcome criteria as designed. The generated NPU boot starts cores 1 through 7 before the scheduler; pinning NPU tasks to core 1 does not reduce that requirement. The host consumes and durably records the terminal zero-length packet when a response occupies a whole number of USB packets, including every 64-byte header at full speed, and reports success only after all output files match, CLOSE reports controller state CLOSED, and the original USB instance remains within the capture deadline. Twenty modeled host cases exercise those boundaries and the actual supervisor (checks/npu-board-capture.py). Retain resources for the prescribed whole-board power removal and stop communication after the first failure; CLOSE stops the NPU locally and USB0 remains active until the 20-second session deadline. Sources of unproven items: the 2 ms settle after domain ON has no pinned source (kept from the controller, to be measured); words 0xc00-0xc10 of the domain-4 delay row are absent from the PCK-600 manual.
